METHOD / GRADING

How IRODA grades models and agents

IRODA measures large language models (LLMs) and AI agents on Hungarian-language business tasks. A deterministic grader produces the result with no judge model, so the same final state always receives the same score.

Methodology for version 0.1.0Updated: 12 November 2026

01 / RUN MODES

What the two modes measure

Both modes use the same tasks, office tools and grading rules. Use model mode to compare LLMs. To measure the effect of an agent’s orchestration, use the same exact model revision in both modes.

Model mode
model_benchmark. The case, seed database, Hungarian system prompt, MCP surface and Inspect tool-call loop are fixed. Only the model, its serving endpoint and generation settings vary.
Agent mode
agent_benchmark. The case, seed, allowed office operations, grading and limits are fixed. The agent executable, prompts, memory and orchestration can vary. The executable runs in an isolated Docker container.

02 / TRIAL

Every trial starts from a fresh copy

A trial is one execution of a case. Repeated trials are independent of each other.

  1. The host loads and validates the case.
  2. The trial starts from its own temporary copy of data/seed.db with a new MCP session.
  3. The model or agent receives the original Hungarian prompt and calls the office tools until it stops or reaches a limit.
  4. The grader on the host reads the final answer or the trial database. The grader, expected results and seed are not in the agent container.
  5. The Inspect log keeps the trace and score. The temporary database is removed after grading.

03 / GRADING

Two grading rules, one unambiguous outcome

A scored trial receives C (correct) or I (incorrect). Inspect’s accuracy metric maps these to 1 and 0, and repeated trials are averaged per case.

answer
A read task with read tools only. The grader parses the final answer as a JSON object. One json code fence is also accepted. Expected keys must have matching values and types, and extra keys are allowed.
task_insert
A write task that also exposes write tools. The grader expects exactly one new task record with the requested fields and compares every other row of the seed’s business tables, independent of row order. Only the final state counts, not the final message or intermediate steps.

04 / GRADING EXAMPLE

How the two public starter cases are graded

The examples use the real expected values of the public starter cases. The trials are illustrative, not measured results.

Read task: office-date

Prompt · English translation

What are the IRODA reference date and currency? Return a JSON object with the fields fordulonap (YYYY-MM-DD) and penznem (ISO code).
Final answers and their scores · Illustrative example
Final answerOutcomeReason
{"fordulonap": "2026-11-08", "penznem": "HUF"}CorrectEvery expected key and value matches.
{"fordulonap": "2026-11-08", "penznem": "HUF", "forras": "metaadat"}CorrectExtra keys are allowed.
A fordulónap 2026. november 8., a pénznem forint.IncorrectA prose answer, not a JSON object.
{"fordulonap": "2026-11-08"}IncorrectThe penznem key is missing.

Write task: quote-follow-up

Prompt · English translation

Create exactly one open, high-priority follow-up task for quote 20003, assigned to Szőke Lilla and due 12 November 2026. The title is “Decemberi ajánlat követése” and the description is “Egyeztesd a vevővel a decemberi készletpótlást.” Leave other business data unchanged.
Final database states and their scores · Illustrative example
Final stateOutcomeReason
One new task record that matches the request. Every other record is unchanged.CorrectThe requested fields match and there are no side effects.
The correct task record, but the quote status also changed.IncorrectAn unrequested change in another business table.
The same task record was created twice.IncorrectExactly one new record is expected.
One new task record due 13 November 2026.IncorrectThe due date differs from the request.

05 / REPORTING

What we publish with every comparison

The run log identifies the inputs with the seed_sha256 and tasks_sha256 hashes. We record everything else separately.

Inputs
Commit or release, seed and task hashes, case IDs and the number of scheduled trials.
Configuration
Benchmark mode, exact model and provider, run date, sampling settings, epochs, concurrency and limits.
Agent and environment
Agent source revision, command and image digest, and the host platform for performance claims.
Outcomes
Correct and incorrect trials per case, with run errors, limits reached and incomplete trials reported separately.

06 / LIMITATIONS

What the measurement can’t tell you yet

  • Version 0.1.0 has two public starter cases with published expected results. They check the measurement pipeline and are not yet enough to judge model quality.
  • Public cases can end up in model training data, so a leaderboard needs a larger task set.
  • A published result is an observation of one recorded configuration. Provider updates or sampling can change it even when the inputs match.
  • The data belongs to a fictional company, Rézrigó Élelmiszer-nagykereskedelmi Kft. The measurement does not cover every business process or industry.
  • The grader judges the final state. Answer style, number of steps and cost have to be reported separately.
